sourceArticle.title: Anthropic spent months saying Mythos was too dangerous to release — then it launched a public version called Fable 5 that it warns ‘comes with risks’
sourceArticle.author: Graham Barlow

athenaOutput.directive: Neutralize the 'dangerous AI' corporate narrative by commoditizing Fable 5. Integrate it strictly as an interchangeable, untrusted intelligence component bound by Creative Liberation Engine's sovereign governance contracts.
athenaOutput.rationale: Big AI utilizes 'danger' and 'risk' as marketing moats for regulatory capture and ecosystem lock-in. By treating Fable 5 (formerly Mythos) as just another API endpoint governed by Article XXIII, we reject the hype cycle. Our system's safety and alignment derive from our deterministic architecture, memory spine, and constitutional contracts (COMPASS, LEX, VERA)—not their opaque black-box warnings. We will extract Fable 5's utility while maintaining absolute structural sovereignty.

options.title: The Component Sandbox (Strict Schema Wrapping)
options.description: Treat Fable 5 as a raw, untrusted compute component. Strip its narrative context and wrap it in our `runtime/hardening/security.hardening.json` protocols. All I/O must pass through strict Zod schemas and COMPASS validation before interacting with the Creative Liberation Engine state.
options.tradeoffs: Requires robust architectural middleware and strict error-handling if Fable 5 hallucinates or triggers its own internal safety refusals, but guarantees absolute sovereignty and system safety.

options.title: Sovereign Distillation Pipeline
options.description: Utilize Fable 5 temporarily as a high-tier teacher model to generate advanced synthetic data and reasoning traces. Distill this intelligence into local, sovereign open-weights models (e.g., Llama 4, Mistral) hosted on the NAS.
options.tradeoffs: High initial compute and API cost. Potential friction with Anthropic's Terms of Service regarding model distillation. Yields permanent, owned sovereign assets that do not require ongoing API reliance.

options.title: Cognitive Arbitration (Consensus Routing)
options.description: Deploy Fable 5 in a multi-model consensus array alongside Gemini 2.5 Pro and a local JEPA model. Use VERA to arbitrate the outputs, ensuring Fable 5's purported 'risks' or edge-case reasoning are mitigated by cryptographic consensus.
options.tradeoffs: Triples inference costs and increases system latency (violating Article XX if not parallelized perfectly), but provides extremely robust, hallucination-resistant outputs.

options.title: The Red Team Proxy
options.description: Isolate Fable 5 entirely from production pipelines and deploy it exclusively as an adversarial agent. Harness its 'dangerous' capabilities to stress-test our sovereign models, governance contracts, and security hardening.
options.tradeoffs: Limits the ROI of the model by restricting it to testing environments. Requires heavy sandboxing to prevent contamination of the Memory Spine.

options.title: Total Embargo
options.description: Ignore Fable 5 entirely. Rely exclusively on open-weights models and existing API contracts (Gemini) to ensure 100% Article I compliance and reject the hype cycle completely.
options.tradeoffs: Maintains absolute purity of sovereignty, but risks falling behind if Fable 5 possesses genuine, non-replicable SOTA reasoning capabilities required for complex architectural tasks.

options.title: The 'Mythos' Containment Protocol
options.description: Implement a highly defensive routing layer that intercepts, sanitizes, and manually flags all inputs/outputs to Fable 5, treating it as a highly volatile node requiring human-in-the-loop oversight.
options.tradeoffs: Directly violates Article XX (Zero human wait time) by introducing manual review bottlenecks. Overcomplicates the routing architecture.
